faq: Does retargeting need a pixel on my site?
Yes, a pixel or tag has to be recording visits first. If yours is missing or broken, we add or repair it as part of the work, and we explain that audiences take a few days to fill.
How big does my traffic need to be?
Platforms need a few hundred people in an audience before ads run well. If your traffic is small, we use wider windows and combine audiences so ads can still deliver.
Is retargeting allowed with privacy laws?
It is allowed when you follow the rules. We use only the platform's standard audiences, never scraped or bought lists, and we ask that your site shows a cookie notice where your region requires one.
Will people feel followed around the internet?
We prevent that with frequency limits, buyer exclusions and a short time window per message. The goal is a helpful reminder or a clear offer, not the same ad many times a day.

desc:
Retargeting ads for store visitors show a helpful reminder to people who already looked at your products but left without buying. Ecom Swift LLC builds the audiences, ads and frequency limits inside your own ad accounts.

## What is retargeting and how does it work?

Retargeting is advertising aimed at people who have already visited your website or interacted with your social pages. A small piece of tracking code records who viewed which products, who added something to a cart and who bought. The ad platform then lets you show a tailored ad to each of those groups.

The reason it matters is simple: most visitors do not buy on the first visit. They compare prices, get interrupted or wait for payday. Retargeting keeps your store in their mind while they decide, at a much lower cost than finding a brand new stranger.

## Why the right message for each stage matters

A person who glanced at one product needs something different from a person who reached checkout and stopped. The first may need to see reviews, delivery details or other items. The second may only need a reminder and an answer to a worry about shipping or returns. Sending both people the same ad wastes the opportunity.

Frequency matters just as much. Too many views of the same ad feel like being followed, and people start to dislike the brand. A limit on how often each person sees an ad, and a window after which they stop, keeps retargeting useful rather than irritating.

## What a well-built retargeting setup includes

- Audiences for all site visitors, product viewers and cart starters.
- Time windows for each audience, so recent visitors get priority.
- Exclusion of past buyers, unless you want to promote a repeat product.
- A separate message for each stage of the buying journey.
- Dynamic catalog ads that show the exact products someone viewed.
- A frequency limit to prevent overexposure.
- A tracking check, so each audience fills from accurate events.
- Respect for cookie consent and the data rules of each platform.
- A review after the first week, to see which stage responds.
- Optional email list audiences for customers who gave consent.

## How we set it up

First we confirm that your pixel or tag records the right events on your site, since audiences are only as good as the data behind them. If something is missing, we point it out before building. We then create the audiences in your ad account, group them by intent, and write or arrange the ads for each group.

The Basic package covers one platform with an all-visitors audience, past buyers excluded, a few ads and a frequency limit. Standard adds product viewer and cart starter audiences, more ads and a week-one review. Premium builds several time-based audiences, adds catalog ads showing viewed products, covers up to three platforms and finishes with a written review and a handover call. Extra audiences, a creative refresh and an email list audience can be added to any package.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Segment visitors by how close they came to buying.
- Exclude people who bought recently.
- Keep ads helpful: answer doubts about shipping, returns and fit.
- Refresh the creative regularly so it does not go stale.
- Honor cookie consent choices on your site.

**Avoid:**
- Showing the same ad to everyone for months.
- Retargeting with no frequency limit.
- Building an audience too small for the platform to deliver to.
- Using sensitive information about visitors in ad wording.
- Assuming retargeting alone can replace attracting new customers.

## Who it is for

This service suits an online store with steady visitors but many abandoned carts. It suits a service business whose website brings in traffic that rarely fills in the enquiry form. It also suits a brand that already runs ads to new people and wants to make the most of those visits.

## What we need and how to start

We need access to your ad account as a partner or team member, and to your website or store so we can check the tracking, never your passwords. Send any existing ads or product images you want us to use, and tell us about offers or delivery promises you can honestly stand behind. Traffic volume affects how quickly audiences fill, and low traffic simply means a slower start. We tell you honestly where your site stands before we build.
